Required for Honobia Creek, Three Rivers and Herron Family WMAs and OLAP properties. Nonresidents must buy annually with no exemptions; lifetime licence holders are NOT exempt. Residents 17 and under or 64 and over are exempt.
Required for non-hunting, non-fishing use of Department-owned areas such as birdwatching or photography, unless the holder has a current hunting or fishing licence.
Required in addition to HIP to hunt sandhill cranes.
Required in addition to a hunting licence; included in the Sports Pac.
Required in addition to a hunting licence; included in the Sports Pac.
General or controlled bear tag; included in the Sports Pac.
Included in the Sports Pac.
Required for upland game birds; a youth version exists for ages 12-17.
Oregon's state waterfowl validation. First-of-state OR duck stamp issued 1984; confidence on first year medium (collector first-of-state gallery).
Fee pheasant permit for western Oregon release sites.
Endorsement bundled with combination, Pioneer and youth licences; also sold per day.
Application for Oregon controlled hunts; the first application change per hunt series is free.
Allocated through the application system using preference points; remaining permits are sold first-come afterwards.
Premium units; 50 percent of tags go to highest point holders and 50 percent to a weighted random draw.
Several remaining or over-the-counter elk permits are listed each year, including unlimited archery and late any-bull categories.
Premium limited-entry units including Book Cliffs, Henry Mountains and Wasatch.
Utah residents only. Covers buck deer, buck pronghorn, bull elk, bull moose, desert bighorn ram, Rocky Mountain bighorn ram, bison, mountain goat, black bear and wild turkey.
Nonrefundable per-species application fee; hunters may apply for multiple species in the same year.
State waterfowl stamp. First-of-state UT duck stamp issued 1986; confidence on first year medium (collector first-of-state gallery).
Transport tag issued with the big game licence package; multi-season deer tags are also sold.
Transport tag issued with the big game licence package; multi-season elk tags are also sold.
Turkey requires a transport tag and cannot be hunted on an authorisation number alone.
Required for migratory bird hunting; included in the Guard free licensing package.

addon_name: Migratory Bird Authorization and Harvest Record Card
notes: Migratory birds cannot be hunted on an authorisation number alone - the Authorization and Harvest Record Card is required.
Required for released pheasant sites in western Washington; a 3-day version bundled with small game also exists.
Application for Washington special hunt permits and raffles (deer, elk, moose, goat).
State waterfowl stamp. First-of-state WA duck stamp issued 1986; confidence on first year medium (collector first-of-state gallery).
Included with WDFW licence purchases for access to WDFW-managed lands. Does not replace the Discover Pass on other state-managed lands.
First-of-state HI duck stamp issued 1996, the last state to issue one. Confidence medium (collector first-of-state gallery). Other Hawaii licence and permit products were not researched in this pass.
First-of-state NE duck stamp issued 1991. Confidence medium (collector first-of-state gallery). Other Nebraska licence and permit products were not researched in this pass.
First-of-state NV duck stamp issued 1979. Confidence medium (collector first-of-state gallery). Other Nevada licence and permit products were not researched in this pass.
First-of-state NM duck stamp issued 1991. Confidence medium (collector first-of-state gallery). Other New Mexico licence and permit products were not researched in this pass.

First-of-state ND duck stamp issued 1982; the first 20,000 were sold with a print to collectors and numbers 20,001-150,000 were sold to hunters. Confidence medium (collector first-of-state gallery). Other North Dakota licence and permit products were not researched in this pass.
First-of-state SD duck stamp issued 1976. Confidence medium (collector first-of-state gallery). Other South Dakota licence and permit products were not researched in this pass.

Required for game mammal hunting and bundled automatically into every Hawaii hunting licence. Printed as a colour image on the electronic licence; historically endorsed across the front and affixed to the paper licence.
Required of anyone hunting game birds in the established season - pheasant, chukar, francolin, quail, dove and turkey. Purchased alongside the annual licence.
Required for axis deer; Lanai axis deer are lottery-permit only. Axis deer were introduced to Molokai in 1868 and later to Maui and Lanai.
Free with an out-of-state hunter education card or a Hawaii hunting licence issued before 1 July 1990. Required before a first-time nonresident may buy a licence.
Required of all hunters to hunt waterfowl; not required during the spring light goose conservation season. Now issued electronically. First-of-state ND duck stamp issued 1982.
Issued by lottery. Residents in the armed forces stationed outside ND may receive a regular deer gun licence without entering the lottery.
Lottery-issued. Bow tags must be printed and mailed from the main NDGF office.
Lottery-allocated.
Once-in-a-lifetime licence; remains available to armed forces licence holders.

Required of all hunters pursuing small game and, with exceptions, big game. Landowners on limited landowner permits for antelope, deer, elk or turkey are exempt, as are 64-and-older veteran and 69-and-older senior permit holders.
Second stamp required in addition to the Habitat Stamp for waterfowl hunters. First-of-state NE duck stamp issued 1991.
Species-specific permit; a small game hunt permit is NOT required for big game. Landowner and youth rates apply. Some units are draw-allocated with a $7 application fee.
Resident, nonresident, youth and landowner rates. Nonresidents may buy up to 2 fall and 3 spring permits.
Draw application fee applies.
Standard nonresident elk permits are not sold; nonresidents qualify only as landowners within a designated elk management zone.
Species-specific big game permit.
Lottery entry sold as single-entry and multiple-entry; a Combo lottery entry is also offered.
Required of all hunters, anglers and trappers 18 and older. Funds habitat protection and public land access. You cannot legally hunt without it.
Required for hunting on US Forest Service or Bureau of Land Management land. Free resident licences for those 70 and older do not require it.
Species licence bought on top of the base game-hunting licence; standard and draw paths exist. Junior deer licences are reduced fee.
Draw-allocated; junior elk licences are reduced fee.
Draw hunt. An off-range senior hunt requires applicants to be 70 or older on the opening day.
NMDGF certification required before applying for MI-only pronghorn, oryx, elk or deer draw hunts.
Deer, elk, pronghorn and bighorn sheep are all draw-only. Mountain lion is available over the counter. A hunting licence alone does not confer big game privileges.
Required under NRS 502.300, which makes it unlawful to hunt certain migratory game birds without the stamp. First-of-state NV duck stamp issued 1979.
Fee to hunt certain upland game birds under NRS 502.292, with documentation-of-payment requirements. A percentage funds upland game bird protection and propagation projects.
Allows private landowners to sell big game tags for their property, typically antlered elk, deer and pronghorn.
Non-refundable $5 fee on each tag application, directable to predator management or to non-predatory wildlife habitat and research.

Required of anyone 18 or over applying for or buying a hunting, fishing or trapping licence. One per licence year. Not required for 1-day small game, youth, landowner, reduced-fee disabled licences or preference points.
Required separately - combination licences grant fishing and small game privileges but do NOT include this certificate. Exempt from the $6 legislative surcharge.
First-of-state SD duck stamp issued 1976.

Purchased or awarded per species per season. Elk, mountain goat and bighorn sheep award one point per unsuccessful application and carry a $10 nonrefundable application fee. Free for limited access permits and youth 15 or under.
Also authorises unprotected species through 31 Jan, provided the licensee retains the top portion of the licence.
